<details class="result-group" id="theorem-7-1-consistency-of-least-squares">
<summary><span>Theorem 7.1 consistency of least squares</span><span class="result-count">3 endpoints</span></summary>
<div class="result-body">
<div class="textbook-statement"><p>Under Assumption 7.1, $\hat{\beta} \xrightarrow{p} \beta$ as $n \to \infty$</p></div>
<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-olsbetastar-stack-tendstoinmeasure-beta">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">theorem</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.olsBetaStar_stack_tendstoInMeasure_beta</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p><strong>Consistency of the totalized least-squares estimator.</strong>
Under the moment-level assumptions above and the linear model <code>yᵢ = Xᵢ·β + eᵢ</code>,
the total OLS estimator <code>β̂*ₙ := (Xᵀ X)⁺ Xᵀ y</code> (using <code>Matrix.nonsingInv</code>)
converges in probability to <code>β</code>.</p>
<p>Proof chain:
* F2: <code>β̂*ₙ = Q̂ₙ⁻¹ *ᵥ ĝₙ(y)</code> pointwise.
* F3: <code>ĝₙ(y) = Q̂ₙ β + ĝₙ(e)</code> under the linear model.
* F6: residual <code>β̂*ₙ − β − Q̂ₙ⁻¹ *ᵥ ĝₙ(e) →ₚ 0</code> (it vanishes on the invertibility
  event, whose complement has measure → 0 by F4).
* Task 11: <code>Q̂ₙ⁻¹ *ᵥ ĝₙ(e) →ₚ 0</code>.
* F5 (twice): residual + error term + β →ₚ 0 + 0 + β = β.
* Pointwise algebra: the sum equals <code>β̂*ₙ</code>. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ {Ω : Type u_1} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {k : Type u_3} [inst : Fintype k] [inst_1 : DecidableEq k]
  {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} [inst_2 : MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure μ] {X : Nat → Ω → k → Real}
  {e y : Nat → Ω → Real} (β : k → Real),
  HansenEconometrics.LeastSquaresConsistencyConditions μ X e →
    (∀ (i : Nat) (ω : Ω), Eq (y i ω) (instHAdd.hAdd (dotProduct (X i ω) β) (e i ω))) →
      MeasureTheory.TendstoInMeasure μ
        (fun n ω =&gt;
          HansenEconometrics.olsBetaStar (HansenEconometrics.stackRegressors X n ω)
            (HansenEconometrics.stackOutcomes y n ω))
        Filter.atTop fun x =&gt; β</code></pre>
</details>
<details class="dependency-list"><summary>Direct statement dependencies (4)</summary><ul><li><code>HansenEconometrics.LeastSquaresConsistencyConditions</code></li><li><code>HansenEconometrics.olsBetaStar</code></li><li><code>HansenEconometrics.stackOutcomes</code></li><li><code>HansenEconometrics.stackRegressors</code></li></ul></details>
<p class="declaration-meta"><a href="https://github.com/apoorvalal/lean-hansen-econometrics/blob/main/HansenEconometrics/Chapter7Asymptotics/Consistency.lean#L1128">HansenEconometrics/Chapter7Asymptotics/Consistency.lean:1128</a></p>
</div>
</details>

<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p><strong>Theorem 7.1 ordinary-OLS-on-nonsingular-samples consistency.</strong></p>

<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-scoreproj-samplecrossmoment-tendstoindistribution-gaussian-cov-all">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">theorem</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.scoreProj_sampleCrossMoment_tendstoInDistribution_gaussian_cov_all</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p><strong>Hansen Theorem 7.2, all scalar projections with <code>Ω</code>.</strong></p>
<p>This packages the scalar projection family used by the vector-valued
Cramér-Wold theorem below: for every fixed direction <code>a</code>, the scalar projection
of <code>√n · ĝₙ(e)</code> has Gaussian limit with variance <code>a' Ω a</code>. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ {Ω : Type u_1} {Ω&#x27; : Type u_2} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {mΩ&#x27; : MeasurableSpace Ω&#x27;} {k : Type u_3} [inst : Fintype k]
  [inst_1 : DecidableEq k] {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} [inst_2 : MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
  {ν : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω&#x27;} [inst_3 : MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure ν] {X : Nat → Ω → k → Real}
  {e : Nat → Ω → Real},
  HansenEconometrics.SampleCLTAssumption72 μ X e →
    ∀ {Z : (k → Real) → Ω&#x27; → Real},
      (∀ (a : k → Real),
          ProbabilityTheory.HasLaw (Z a)
            (ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal 0 (dotProduct a ((HansenEconometrics.scoreCovMat μ X e).mulVec a)).toNNReal)
            ν) →
        ∀ (a : k → Real),
          MeasureTheory.TendstoInDistribution
            (fun n ω =&gt;
              dotProduct
                (instHSMul.hSMul n.cast.sqrt
                  (HansenEconometrics.sampleCrossMoment (HansenEconometrics.stackRegressors X n ω)
                    (HansenEconometrics.stackErrors e n ω)))
                a)
            Filter.atTop (Z a) (fun x =&gt; μ) ν</code></pre>
</details>

<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-scorevector-samplecrossmoment-tendstoindistribution-multivariategaussian">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">theorem</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.scoreVector_sampleCrossMoment_tendstoInDistribution_multivariateGaussian</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p><strong>Hansen Theorem 7.2, vector score CLT in Chapter 7 function-vector notation.</strong></p>
<p>This is the public Chapter 7 score CLT: <code>√n · ĝₙ(e)</code> converges to the
multivariate Gaussian score vector. The limit random variable is the coordinate
view of the Gaussian on <code>EuclideanSpace ℝ k</code>, matching the rest of the chapter's
<code>k → ℝ</code> vector notation. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ {Ω : Type u_1} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {k : Type u_3} [inst : Fintype k] [inst_1 : DecidableEq k]
  {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} [inst_2 : MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {X : Nat → Ω → k → Real}
  {e : Nat → Ω → Real},
  HansenEconometrics.ScoreCLTConditions μ X e →
    MeasureTheory.TendstoInDistribution
      (fun n ω =&gt;
        instHSMul.hSMul n.cast.sqrt
          (HansenEconometrics.sampleCrossMoment (HansenEconometrics.stackRegressors X n ω)
            (HansenEconometrics.stackErrors e n ω)))
      Filter.atTop (fun z =&gt; z.ofLp) (fun x =&gt; μ)
      (ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian 0 (HansenEconometrics.scoreCovMat μ X e))</code></pre>
</details>

<div class="declaration-doc"><p><strong>Theorem 7.2 finite second-moment face.</strong></p>
<p>Every entry of the score second-moment matrix

textbook statement that the asymptotic covariance matrix <code>Ω</code> has finite
entries under Assumption 7.2. </p></div>

        (fun ω =&gt; instHMul.hMul (instHSMul.hSMul (e 0 ω) (X 0 ω) j) (instHSMul.hSMul (e 0 ω) (X 0 ω) l)) μ</code></pre>
</details>

<details class="result-group" id="theorem-7-3">
<summary><span>Theorem 7.3</span><span class="result-count">6 endpoints</span></summary>
<div class="result-body">
<div class="textbook-statement"><p>Under Assumption 7.2, $\sqrt n(\hat\beta-\beta)\xrightarrow{d}N(0,Q_{XX}^{-1}\Omega Q_{XX}^{-1})$.</p></div>
<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-scoreproj-olsbetastar-tendstoindistribution-gaussian-cov-all">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">theorem</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.scoreProj_olsBetaStar_tendstoInDistribution_gaussian_cov_all</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p><strong>Hansen Theorem 7.3, all scalar projections for totalized OLS with <code>Ω</code>.</strong></p>
<p>For every fixed direction <code>a</code>, the scaled totalized OLS error has Gaussian
limit with asymptotic variance <code>((Q⁻¹)'a)' Ω ((Q⁻¹)'a)</code>. This is the complete
projection-family form currently available before the vector/Cramér-Wold
wrapper is formalized. </p></div>

score vector. This theorem discharges the vector score CLT using the
Cramér-Wold score theorem above. </p></div>

<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-olsbetastar">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">def</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.olsBetaStar</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p><strong>Star primitive</strong>: totalized OLS coefficient that is defined on every design matrix.</p>
<p>Uses <code>Matrix.nonsingInv</code> in place of the typeclass inverse <code>⅟(Xᵀ * X)</code>, so it is a genuine
function with no typeclass precondition.  On <strong>singular</strong> designs <code>(Xᵀ * X)⁻¹ = 0</code> by
definition, so <code>olsBetaStar X y = 0</code>; on <strong>nonsingular</strong> designs it agrees with <code>olsBeta</code>
(see <code>olsBetaStar_eq_olsBeta</code>).</p>
<p>Role in the project architecture:
- <strong>Chapters 3–5</strong> use <code>olsBeta</code> (typeclass inverse) for finite-sample algebra.
- <strong>Chapter 7+</strong> use <code>olsBetaStar</code> as the proof engine for asymptotic results, where
  nonsingularity holds only a.s. and cannot be supplied as a global typeclass.
- Textbook-facing statements that a reader would want to cite use <code>olsBetaOrZero</code>
  (Chapter 7), which is provably equal to <code>olsBetaStar</code> (see <code>olsBetaOrZero_eq_olsBetaStar</code>). </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">{n : Type u_1} → {k : Type u_2} → [Fintype n] → [Fintype k] → [DecidableEq k] → Matrix n k Real → (n → Real) → k → Real</code></pre>
</details>

<p class="declaration-meta"><a href="https://github.com/apoorvalal/lean-hansen-econometrics/blob/main/HansenEconometrics/Chapter3LeastSquaresAlgebra.lean#L34">HansenEconometrics/Chapter3LeastSquaresAlgebra.lean:34</a></p>
</div>
</details>
<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-olsbetaorzero">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">def</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.olsBetaOrZero</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p><strong>OrZero primitive</strong>: textbook-facing totalization of ordinary OLS.</p>
<p>Branches explicitly on <code>IsUnit (Xᵀ * X).det</code>:
- <strong>nonsingular</strong>: returns the ordinary <code>olsBeta X y</code> (typeclass inverse);
- <strong>singular</strong>: returns <code>0</code>.</p>
<p>This makes <code>olsBetaOrZero</code> suitable for textbook-facing statements that a reader would
want to cite directly (e.g., consistency, asymptotic normality headlines), because the
formula matches ordinary OLS on the high-probability nonsingularity event.</p>
<p>For proofs, the equivalent <code>olsBetaStar</code> (a Star primitive using <code>Matrix.nonsingInv</code>) is
typically more convenient; the bridge <code>olsBetaOrZero_eq_olsBetaStar</code> (private <code>@[simp]</code>)
connects the two. See the <strong>Star / OrZero totalization convention</strong> in <code>AGENTS.md</code> for
the full architecture. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">{n : Type u_1} → {k : Type u_2} → [Fintype n] → [Fintype k] → [DecidableEq k] → Matrix n k Real → (n → Real) → k → Real</code></pre>
</details>

<p class="declaration-meta"><a href="https://github.com/apoorvalal/lean-hansen-econometrics/blob/main/HansenEconometrics/Chapter7Asymptotics/Basic.lean#L75">HansenEconometrics/Chapter7Asymptotics/Basic.lean:75</a></p>
</div>
</details>
</div>
</details>

<details class="result-group" id="theorem-7-9">

<div class="result-body">

<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-nonlinearfunction-olsbetastar-delta-tendstoindistribution-gaussian">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">theorem</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.nonlinearFunction_olsBetaStar_delta_tendstoInDistribution_gaussian</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p><strong>Hansen Theorem 7.9, nonlinear Delta-method wrapper for totalized OLS.</strong></p>
<p>This is the Chapter 7-facing nonlinear packaging now that the Chapter 6
Delta-method/law-relabeling layer is available.  If <code>Yₙ</code> is the scaled nonlinear
statistic and it differs from the derivative image of
<code>√n(β̂*ₙ - β)</code> by <code>oₚ(1)</code>, then <code>Yₙ</code> has the named Gaussian law of that derivative
image.  Concrete transforms <code>r(β̂ₙ)</code> discharge <code>hrem</code> from the usual
Fréchet-derivative remainder. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ {Ω : Type u_1} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {k : Type u_3} [inst : Fintype k] [inst_1 : DecidableEq k]
  {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} [inst_2 : MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {X : Nat → Ω → k → Real}
  {e y : Nat → Ω → Real} {q : Type u_4} [inst_3 : Fintype q] [inst_4 : DecidableEq q],
  HansenEconometrics.ScoreCLTConditions μ X e →
    ∀ (β : k → Real) (R : Matrix q k Real),
      (∀ (i : Nat) (ω : Ω), Eq (y i ω) (instHAdd.hAdd (dotProduct (X i ω) β) (e i ω))) →
        ∀ {Y : Nat → Ω → EuclideanSpace Real q},
          (∀ (n : Nat), AEMeasurable (Y n) μ) →
            (MeasureTheory.TendstoInMeasure μ
                (fun n ω =&gt;
                  instHSub.hSub (Y n ω)
                    (ContinuousLinearMap.funLike.coe (HansenEconometrics.matrixContinuousLinearMap R)
                      {
                        ofLp :=
                          instHSMul.hSMul n.cast.sqrt
                            (instHSub.hSub
                              (HansenEconometrics.olsBetaStar (HansenEconometrics.stackRegressors X n ω)
                                (HansenEconometrics.stackOutcomes y n ω))
                              β) }))
                Filter.atTop fun x =&gt; 0) →
              ProbabilityTheory.HasLaw
                  (fun z =&gt;
                    ContinuousLinearMap.funLike.coe (HansenEconometrics.matrixContinuousLinearMap R)
                      { ofLp := (Matrix.inv.inv (HansenEconometrics.popGram μ X)).mulVec z.ofLp })
                  (ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian 0
                    (Matrix.instHMulOfFintypeOfMulOfAddCommMonoid.hMul
                      (Matrix.instHMulOfFintypeOfMulOfAddCommMonoid.hMul R (HansenEconometrics.heteroAsymCov μ X e))
                      R.transpose))
                  (ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian 0 (HansenEconometrics.scoreCovMat μ X e)) →
                MeasureTheory.TendstoInDistribution Y Filter.atTop (fun z =&gt; z) (fun x =&gt; μ)
                  (ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian 0
                    (Matrix.instHMulOfFintypeOfMulOfAddCommMonoid.hMul
                      (Matrix.instHMulOfFintypeOfMulOfAddCommMonoid.hMul R (HansenEconometrics.heteroAsymCov μ X e))
                      R.transpose))</code></pre>
</details>

<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p><strong>Hansen Theorem 7.11, generic nonlinear scalar t-statistic.</strong></p>
<p>If the scaled scalar plug-in error has a distributional limit and the nonlinear
standard error converges in probability to a positive constant, then the
studentized nonlinear scalar statistic converges to the corresponding ratio

<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-symmetricci-coverage-of-abs-tstat-nonpos-tendsto-zero">

<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p><strong>Hansen Theorem 7.12, probabilistic symmetric confidence-interval coverage bridge.</strong></p>
<p>This version removes the pointwise eventual standard-error positivity shortcut:
it is enough that the nonpositive-standard-error event has probability tending
to zero. The interval event and the absolute-t-statistic event can then differ
only on a negligible bad set. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ {Ω : Type u_1} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} [inst : MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
  {θ crit : Real} {θhat se : Nat → Ω → Real} {root : Nat → Real},
  Filter.Eventually (fun n =&gt; Real.instLT.lt 0 (root n)) Filter.atTop →
    Filter.Tendsto (fun n =&gt; MeasureTheory.Measure.instFunLike.coe μ (setOf fun ω =&gt; Real.instLE.le (se n ω) 0))
        Filter.atTop (nhds 0) →
      MeasureTheory.TendstoInDistribution
          (fun n ω =&gt; abs (instHDiv.hDiv (instHMul.hMul (root n) (instHSub.hSub (θhat n ω) θ)) (se n ω))) Filter.atTop
          (fun x =&gt; abs x) (fun x =&gt; μ) (ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal 0 1) →
        Eq
            (MeasureTheory.Measure.instFunLike.coe
              (MeasureTheory.Measure.map (fun x =&gt; abs x) (ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal 0 1))
              (frontier (Set.Iic crit)))
            0 →
          Filter.Tendsto
            (fun n =&gt;
              MeasureTheory.Measure.instFunLike.coe μ
                (setOf fun ω =&gt;
                  Set.instMembership.mem
                    (Set.Icc (instHSub.hSub (θhat n ω) (instHDiv.hDiv (instHMul.hMul crit (se n ω)) (root n)))
                      (instHAdd.hAdd (θhat n ω) (instHDiv.hDiv (instHMul.hMul crit (se n ω)) (root n))))
                    θ))
            Filter.atTop
            (nhds
              (MeasureTheory.Measure.instFunLike.coe
                (MeasureTheory.Measure.map (fun x =&gt; abs x) (ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal 0 1)) (Set.Iic crit)))</code></pre>
</details>

<details class="result-group" id="theorem-7-15">
<summary><span>Theorem 7.15</span><span class="result-count">6 of 8 linked endpoints</span></summary>
<div class="result-body">
<div class="textbook-statement"><p>Under the stated high-moment conditions, $\Pr(T\le x)=\Phi(x)+n^{-1/2}p_1(x)\phi(x)+n^{-1}p_2(x)\phi(x)+o(n^{-1})$; the $n^{-1/2}$ term cancels for symmetric intervals.</p></div>
<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-secondorderedgeworthexpansion-symmetric-interval-scaled-remainder-tendsto-zero">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">theorem</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.SecondOrderEdgeworthExpansion.symmetric_interval_scaled_remainder_tendsto_zero</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p>Symmetric two-sided Edgeworth expansion consequence.</p>
<p>For a symmetric interval, the <code>n^{-1/2}</code> correction cancels when <code>p₁</code> is even
and the density is even, while the odd <code>p₂</code> term contributes twice its positive
cutoff value. This is the formal version of Hansen's explanation after
Theorem 7.15 that two-sided intervals remove the first-order Edgeworth
coverage error. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ {Ω : Type u_1} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} [inst : MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
  {T : Nat → Ω → Real} {baseCDF density p1 p2 : Real → Real},
  HansenEconometrics.SecondOrderEdgeworthExpansion μ T baseCDF density p1 p2 →
    ∀ (c : Real),
      Eq (p1 (Real.instNeg.neg c)) (p1 c) →
        Eq (p2 (Real.instNeg.neg c)) (Real.instNeg.neg (p2 c)) →
          Eq (density (Real.instNeg.neg c)) (density c) →
            Filter.Tendsto
              (fun n =&gt;
                instHMul.hMul n.cast
                  (instHSub.hSub
                    (instHSub.hSub
                      (instHSub.hSub (HansenEconometrics.statisticCDFReal μ T n c)
                        (HansenEconometrics.statisticCDFReal μ T n (Real.instNeg.neg c)))
                      (instHSub.hSub (baseCDF c) (baseCDF (Real.instNeg.neg c))))
                    (instHMul.hMul (Real.instInv.inv n.cast) (instHMul.hMul 2 (instHMul.hMul (p2 c) (density c))))))
              Filter.atTop (nhds 0)</code></pre>
</details>

<details class="result-group" id="theorem-7-16">
<summary><span>Theorem 7.16</span><span class="result-count">6 endpoints</span></summary>
<div class="result-body">
<div class="textbook-statement"><p>If $\mathbb E\lVert X\rVert^r\lt \infty$, then $\max_{1\le i\le n}\lvert\hat e_i-e_i\rvert=o_p(n^{-1/2+1/r})$.</p></div>
<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-scaledmaxresidualerrorstar-tendstoinmeasure-zero-of-scaled-product">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">theorem</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.scaledMaxResidualErrorStar_tendstoInMeasure_zero_of_scaled_product</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p><strong>Hansen Theorem 7.16, max residual rate packaging.</strong></p>
<p>If a deterministic rate scaling sends the product of the maximal row norm and
the totalized coefficient error to zero in probability, then the scaled maximum
residual error is also <code>oₚ(1)</code>.  The remaining textbook-specific work is to
combine this wrapper with the Chapter 6 maximum bound for the regressor row
norm and the Chapter 7 OLS rate. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ {Ω : Type u_1} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {k : Type u_3} [inst : Fintype k] [inst_1 : DecidableEq k]
  {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} [MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure μ] {X : Nat → Ω → k → Real} {e : Nat → Ω → Real}
  (β : k → Real) (scale : Nat → Real),
  (∀ (n : Nat), Real.instLE.le 0 (scale n)) →
    (MeasureTheory.TendstoInMeasure μ
        (fun n ω =&gt;
          instHMul.hMul (scale n)
            (instHMul.hMul
              (instHMul.hMul (Fintype.card k).cast
                (HansenEconometrics.maxRowNorm (HansenEconometrics.stackRegressors X n ω)))
              (Pi.normedRing.norm
                (instHSub.hSub
                  (HansenEconometrics.olsBetaStar (HansenEconometrics.stackRegressors X n ω)
                    (instHAdd.hAdd ((HansenEconometrics.stackRegressors X n ω).mulVec β)
                      (HansenEconometrics.stackErrors e n ω)))
